0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 January 1987, after the draft finalized by the Cordage Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 First published make it up-to-date use. 3.1 The test shall normally

be carried out under prevailing atmospheric conditions. In all cases of dispute, however, tests shall be carried out on samples which have been conditioned for 24 hours in an atmosphere at 65 f 2 percent relative humidity and 27 f 2�C temperature (see IS : 6359-1971t). Where practicable tests shall be made in the standard conditoining atmosphere otherwise, they shall be made as quickly as possible but not exceeding 15 minutes of removal of the test pieces from the conditioning atmosphere. 4. MANUFACTURE

4.1 Jute Fibre - The jute fibre used for the manufacture of pilot lead line shall be true to its type, unadultrated and free from defects and It shall be well carded. shorts.
4.2 Basic Yarn-Jute yarn; 276, tax ( or 8 grist: ), used for making pilot lead line shall be well and evenly spun. It shall be spun with `Z' twist. 4.3 Three-Ply Yarn -Three together in the `S' direction well and evenly spun. basic yarns (see 4.2 ) shall be twisted to form a 3-ply yarn. The yarn shall be to be

4.4 Strands - Five 3-ply yarns shall be laid together in `S' direction form a strand. The strands shall have `Z' lay. The strands shall well formed and free from splices, grooves and sunken yarns. 4.5 Primary Cord - Two strands direction to form a primary cord. 4.6 shall be twisted together It shall be polished.

direction

Three primary cords shall be laid in the `S' a core. The pilot lead line shall be well laid and free from splices, joints and defects.

MARKING 8.1 Each package in a lot shall be marked a) Name of the material, b) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, and c) Length of pilot lead line in the package, d) Net mass of the package, e) Year of manufacture. 8.1.1 Each package may also be marked as required by the buyer. 8.1.2 The package may also be marked with any other marking Mark. with the following:

NOTE -The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard thereunder. conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

APPENDIX ( Table 1 )
METHOD B-l. FOR DETERMINATION

B
OF BREAKING LOAD

APPARATUS

B-l.1 Rope tensile testing machine of appropriate capacity with constant rate of traverse of the straining head of not less than 150 mm per minute or greater than 305 mm per minute. B-2. PROCEDURE B-2.1 Test By Ordinary Grips-Mount each specimen with an initial length of not less than 1 m between the grips of the testing machine. Apply gradually and continuously increasing load until the specimen breaks. If fracture occurs at or near the grips at less than the specified breaking load, disregard the test and take a further test. Accept the test results corresponding to any specimen that fractures through causes attributable to grip damage as meeting the requirements of the specification provided that the load recorded is not less than 95 percent of the minimum specified breaking load. B-2.2 Test the remaining specimens similarly.

B-2.3 Report the lot to be in compliance with the requirements of 5.3 in respect of breaking load if the condition laid down in 9.4 (b) is satisfied.
